question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>18</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>77</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> be a set of integers with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo><</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo><</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>18</mn></msub><mo><</mo><mn>77</mn></math>. Let the set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> contain exactly <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>39</mn></math> elements. Then, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>18</mn></msub></math> is equal to ______.

solution.text:
If we write the elements of \(A+A\), we can certainly find 39 distinct elements as \(1+1,1+a_1, 1+a_2, \ldots .1\) \(+a_{18}, 1+77, a_1+77, a_2+77, \ldots \ldots a_{18}+77,77+77\). It means all other sums are already present in these 39 values, which is only possible in case when all numbers are in A.P.
Let the common difference be ' \(d\) '.
\(77=1+19 d \Rightarrow d=4\)
So, \(\sum_{i=1}^{18} a_1=\frac{18}{2}\left[2 a_1+17 d\right]=9[10+68]=702\)
